title: Span Balance Standup Snapshot — 2028-09-23
content:
Context and purpose:
This note captures the standup discussion on span sampling balance, the recent cost telemetry spike we investigated, and short-term dashboard changes. Treat as an operational snapshot (not final runbook). Planning to iterate and fold into the sampling playbook after next sprint.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (notes)
- Alejandro Ruiz
- Priya Sharma
- Noah Patel
- Jeremy Kwan (briefly)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Observed a 42% increase in span ingest volume from two API routes since the kernel-selection rollout on 2028-09-20. Cost telemetry flagged token / span processing as the largest driver of month-to-date spend increase.
- Root cause appears to be a combination of changed request fan-out (more microservice calls) PLUS our default trace sampling not adapting to new per-request span counts.
- Immediate mitigation: lower sampling for non-user-facing internal services and apply prefix caching opt-out to the high-churn endpoints.
- Next sprint: run controlled sampling matrix for three customer tiers and instrument end-to-end span count histogram by route.

Observations / evidence:
- Metric spike timeline:
  - 2028-09-20 02:00 UTC: kernel-selector v2 deployed to canary; by 08:00 UTC sampling/trace pipeline shows 20% more spans/req on canary hosts.
  - 2028-09-21 00:00 UTC: rollout to prod; by 06:00 UTC cost telemetry alerts fired for span-ingest bucket.
  - 2028-09-22 12:00 UTC: cross-checked with request logs; avg spans/request jumped from 4.1 -> 8.9 on two routes (chat-mux, rerank-service).
- Dashboards used: span-ingest-by-route (heatmap), span-size-histogram, sampling-coverage-over-time. Links in linked_artifacts.

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis:
1) Kernel v2 changed how we shard streaming requests; additional internal RPC calls for prefetch and sub-token scheduling doubled internal spans for long-chats.
2) Our default sampling policy (0.25 global, 0.5 for user-facing) assumes bounded spans/req. That assumption broke for long-chat sessions, so effective sampled spans increased total ingress and cost even while sampled fraction remained the same.
3) No guardrail in routing to preferentially reduce sampling on internal-only traces.

Immediate actions taken (today):
- Rolled an emergency sampling override to 0.1 for services tagged "internal" (Alejandro) — implementation: runtime feature flip in trace-profiles service.
- Added a dashboard panel to highlight spans/request per route with 1h and 24h windows (Priya) — temporary tile in ops-board.
- Throttled prefix-cache refresh for chat-mux to reduce prefetch span fan-out (Noah) — config change pushed, monitoring in flight.
- Opened JIRA-OBS-1278 to track follow-ups and assigned owners.

Short-term experiments (next 7 days):
- Sampling matrix: run 4x4 experiment across routes x tiers (global rates: 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5) and measure per-request span count and latency regression. Collab: Priya + Alejandro.
- Endpoint-level histograms: instrument a small patch to emit span_count and longtail_count as tags on existing traces so we can compute distribution without full ingestion. Target deploy: 2028-09-26 (Noah).
- Cost attribution split: add an extra dimension to token-billing pipeline to tag spans_by_kernel and spans_by-prefetch so we can separate kernel-change vs prefetch cost. (Maya)

Dashboard & observability tasks:
- Ops-board: move the new spans/request tile into the top-left, add anomaly-color thresholds (done by Priya).
- Create a cross-team dashboard for platform + product to see customer-visible latency alongside span-cost to support tradeoffs during rollouts. Jira: CONFLUENCE-OBS-4321 doc skeleton created.
- Retention check: confirm whether higher span rates will inflate retention cost; propose a 30-day retention for high-cardinality trace indices as default and move older traces to cold storage. (Runbook note)

Decisions made in-standup:
- Temporary default sampling for internal services reduced to 0.1 until the experiment completes. Decision window: 7 days.
- Instrumentation patch (span_count tag) to be shipped to canary first; if data confirms hypothesis, roll to prod.
- No immediate rollback of kernel-selector v2; prefer to tune sampling and prefetch behavior.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: overly aggressive sampling on internal services could hide cross-service regressions during debugging. Mitigation: keep a small persistent sample (0.005) of internal traces flagged as "forensics-enabled".
- Will reducing sampling affect APM alert quality? We need to validate alert precision/recall during the matrix. (SRE ops)
- Does retention policy change conflict with compliance requirements for enterprises? Loop in compliance before rolling retention defaults.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Alejandro: keep sampling override live and monitor cost delta; EOD 2028-09-24 (status: active).
- Priya: formalize ops-board tile and add SLA mismatch alert (false positives for low sample) — 2028-09-25 (in progress).
- Noah: implement span_count tagging, deploy to canary + smoke test — 2028-09-26 (blocked on small build flake, tracking in GH PR). PR: https://github.com/redwood/trace-profiles/pull/214.
- Maya: update cost-attribution pipeline to add kernel | prefetch split dimension; quick query for yesterday vs baseline — 2028-09-28 (draft schema done).
- Jeremy: advise on whether kernel-selector needs a follow-up to reduce prefetch fan-out — 2028-09-27 (pending).

Notes and raw standup chatter (verbatim fragments):
- "we didn't expect prefetch to open three more rpc hops for long-chats" — Alejandro
- "ops-board showing span surge even for low-traffic tenants — that's the broken interaction" — Priya
- "we should ensure sampling flags can be toggled by tag, not just service name" — Noah

Follow-ups for product & platform stakeholders:
- Product: decide acceptable span-cost vs latency tradeoffs for long-chat flows; include customers with >50k monthly calls in discussion.
- Platform: add a rollout checklist item to simulate worst-case span multiplication before kernel-level rollouts.

Appendix: quick playbook snippets
- Emergency sampling override pattern:
  - Feature flip in trace-profiles: set override by tag (internal:true) -> sample_rate = 0.1
  - Verify with span-ingest-by-route and sampled-trace-checker queries for first 30 mins
  - Revert only after two consecutive days of stable cost and histograms back to baseline

- Developer debugging tips:
  - If a route shows sudden span_count growth, check prefetch traces and rpc fan-out matrix (tools: trace-graph, rpc-call-matrix)
  - Use the persistent forensics sample to rehydrate full traces for at most 2% of requests when needed

End notes:
This doc will be iterated into the sampling playbook and the trace-runbook. If you want a trimmed summary for on-call, I can produce a one-pager. Please add comments inline or ping in slack:#observability if urgent.

-- Maya
